guarantees.claim: secret_key_d is defaulted to secret_key before any conditional override.
guarantees.cond: always (unless overwritten by later conditional assignment)

guarantees.claim: When wipe_secret is asserted, secret_key_d is driven to a vector of 32 copies of wipe_v (`{32{wipe_v}}`), overriding all other updates.

When wipe_secret is deasserted and cfg_block is low, for each word index i from 0 to 31, if reg2hw.key[31-i].qe is true, then secret_key_d[32*i+:32] is updated to conv_endian32(reg2hw.key[31-i].q, key_swap). Words with qe false keep their previous value (from secret_key or prior update).
When wipe_secret is deasserted and cfg_block is asserted, secret_key_d holds its default value (secret_key) and no word‑level update occurs.

assumptions.claim: External logic ensures that cfg_block is deasserted only when the HMAC engine is in Idle state, as indicated by the comment.
assumptions.cond: when an update to secret_key_d via reg2hw is attempted
assumptions.risk: If cfg_block is low while the engine is active, key words can be updated during processing, corrupting the HMAC operation.

assumptions.claim: The register interface asserts reg2hw.key[*].qe only during safe update windows (i.e., when the engine is idle), consistent with the cfg_block assumption.
assumptions.cond: when not in wipe and cfg_block is low
assumptions.risk: A write qualifier asserted during active processing could partially overwrite the key and compromise HMAC integrity.

assumptions.claim: wipe_v is a vector exactly one key word (32 bits) wide, so the replication {32{wipe_v}} correctly fills the 1024‑bit secret_key_d without truncation or zero‑extension.
assumptions.risk: If wipe_v is narrower, zero‑extension may leave part of the key unwiped; if wider, synthesis will error.

assumptions.claim: The function conv_endian32 is combinational and correctly swaps the byte order of a 32‑bit input when key_swap is high.
assumptions.risk: An incorrect endianness swap would propagate a permuted key word into the secret key, breaking the cryptographic usage.

uncertain_points.claim: The wipe construct `{32{wipe_v}}` assumes wipe_v is exactly 32 bits wide (one key word). If wipe_v is wider (e.g., 64 bits), the replicate‑concatenation will mismatch the width of secret_key_d (likely 1024 bits).
uncertain_points.risk: Synthesis can infer an undesired width, potentially leaving parts of the key unwiped or causing an elaboration error.

uncertain_points.claim: When wipe_secret is asserted, the block forces secret_key_d to the wipe value regardless of cfg_block state, possibly allowing a key wipe while the HMAC engine is still active (cfg_block high).
uncertain_points.risk: If the engine continues to use the key after wipe, it will operate on a known constant (wipe_v), potentially leaking information or producing known weak MACs.

uncertain_points.claim: The exact conditions under which cfg_block is asserted must be verified against the HRAC engine state machine to ensure key updates are truly restricted to idle. The comment mentions Idle, but the RTL only uses cfg_block.
uncertain_points.cond: whenever !cfg_block is used to gate the update
uncertain_points.risk: Mismatch between the comment’s idle requirement and the actual cfg_block generation could allow key modifications during active hash operations, compromising integrity.

uncertain_points.claim: secret_key_d is driven combinationally; if the consumer of secret_key_d uses it asynchronously without a qualifying clock edge, transient changes on key words (due to reg2hw update or wipe) could create a temporal window where a hash operation uses a partially updated key.
uncertain_points.cond: when any input to the combinational block changes
uncertain_points.risk: Temporal key corruption or leakage, possibly observable via side‑channel or producing an incorrect MAC.

uncertain_points.claim: The for‑loop iterates from 0 to 31 and indexes reg2hw.key[31-i], assuming the array has exactly 32 entries. If a parameter reduces the array size, the indexing would be out of bounds.
uncertain_points.cond: if the key array width parameter differs from 32
uncertain_points.risk: Out‑of‑bounds access causes elaboration or simulation errors, and a reduced key size would silently alter the intended key update coverage.
